title: Abkhaz and Russian forces open a second front in the Kodori Valley
body:
The Upper Kodori Valley was the only part of Abkhazia that Georgia still controlled before the war. Fighting there lasted from 9 to 12 August 2008. On 9 August monitors of the United Nations Observer Mission in Georgia (UNOMIG) were asked to leave the valley, and Abkhaz forces opened what was described as a second front with artillery and air attacks on the gorge. On 10 August the bombardment continued, and Abkhaz president Sergei Bagapsh gave Georgian forces a deadline to surrender and offered a humanitarian corridor.

On 11 August Abkhaz defence minister Mirab Kishmaria threatened to destroy Georgian forces that did not use the corridor. A deputy defence minister said about 2,500 Georgian soldiers remained in the gorge and about 1,000 civilians had used the corridor. On 12 August the Abkhaz flag was raised over a former Georgian administrative building by noon; Georgia's Deputy Interior Minister Eka Zguladze described the withdrawal as a goodwill gesture. Bagapsh flew into the gorge on 13 August and declared it retaken.

Russian involvement is disputed. Abkhaz officials and Russian General Anatoly Zaitsev said Russia did not take part, while Georgian minister Temur Iakobashvili claimed Russian forces attacked Georgian troops. Reported losses were small: Abkhaz officials reported one killed, Georgia two soldiers killed, and one Russian soldier was reported killed. About 2,000 residents fled the gorge.
